Denis-Ryan, A., Bataille, C. and Jotzo, F. (2016). Managing carbon-intensive materials in a decarbonizing world without a global price on carbon. Climate Policy, 16(sup1), S110-S128. https://doi.org/10.1080/14693062.2016.1176008

NO TECHNOLOGY PARAMETERS EXTRACTED. Policy and benchmarking paper comparing 2050 iron-and-steel and cement production and emissions in 12 Deep Decarbonization Pathways Project (DDPP) country studies with 'best practice' (IEA 2DS) and 'technical limit' benchmarks; most numbers are sector-level or per capita. Route-level emissions intensities it prints (all reprinted literature averages, not technology parameters): current sector average about 1.8 tCO2/t steel; primary production via BF-BOF and DRI-EAF about 2.3 tCO2/t steel (Birat 2010, Carbon Trust 2011, Worrell et al. 2007 and others); secondary EAF about 0.7 tCO2/t steel; 2050 technical-limit primary 0.2-0.4 tCO2/t steel (IPCC AR5, Fischedick et al. 2014); 2050 modelling results 0.7-0.9 tCO2/t steel; DDPP benchmarks 0.47-0.84 tCO2/t steel; DRI uses natural gas (90% globally) or coal (10%). Cement: process emissions about 50%, fuel 40%, electricity 10% of total; IEA 2DS 2050 direct intensity 0.30-0.38 tCO2e/t cement; lowest achievable about 0.24 tCO2/t cement (DDPP benchmark 0.24-0.39); about 0.1 tCO2/t with CCS, bioenergy and low-carbon electricity; China BAT about 0.4, extreme 0.22 tCO2/t cement (Xu et al. 2014). Sector totals: steel 2.8 GtCO2 and cement 2.5 GtCO2 in 2012; per-capita 2050 results 0.28 (DDPP), 0.72 (best practice), 0.21 (technical limit) tCO2/capita.
